statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail steps to 23% because NQ extended the session high by about 88 points over the past hour and holds near that extreme, while Stress eases to 76% as VIX, Treasury yields and crude all decay together.
recommendation: Tail remains inside the watch band, two points below the block threshold. The upward extension and price holding near the session extreme are genuine current amplifiers, but the supporting cross-asset set is decaying rather than aligning: VIX is 15.98 at its session low (-2.50%), the 10-year is 5.234% and the 2-year 4.783% after dovish Fed commentary, and WTI has fallen 3.41% to 89.70. Conflicting regional equity, with Hong Kong down 3% to an 11-week low and the STOXX 600 heading for its worst week since mid-April, raises uncertainty rather than Tail. Stress stays high on a French 10-year at a 2002 peak with the OAT-Bund spread beyond 140 basis points, long-end Treasury yields near 24-year highs, and the September payrolls release at 12:30Z. The flagged window stays narrow, spanning 12:30Z to 15:00Z around the release and the U.S. cash open.
headline: NQ extends to new session highs while VIX, yields and crude all decay into the September payrolls print
body: NQ futures trade 31,002.75 (+0.79%, +242.25) as of 08:17Z inside an overnight range of 30,760.25-31,025.75 against a 30,760.50 prior close; a delayed cross-check at 08:20Z shows 30,992.75 with a 31,026.50 high. The session high extended about 88 points over the past hour, from 30,937.25, and price now sits roughly 23 points below it, so the past hour added genuine directional efficiency rather than the barely-widening drift seen earlier. The band is about 0.86% wide and pullbacks during the European-morning advance have been shallow, which makes price holding near the extreme the clearest live amplifier. What is absent is cross-asset alignment. VIX is 15.98, down 2.50% from a 16.39 close and sitting at its session low. The 10-year Treasury yield is 5.234% against a 5.238% prior close in a 5.231-5.262 band, well below Thursday's 5.345% print, the highest since 2002; the 2-year is 4.783% against 4.787% after posting its largest daily decline since July on dovish Fed commentary. H.15 constant-maturity data for September 30 shows 4.88% at 2 years and 5.29% at 10 years. October Fed hike odds are priced near 30%, down from about 70% on Monday. Crude has fallen materially further: WTI is 89.70 (-3.41%) and Brent 99.87 (-2.39%), having held above 102 during the Asian session, as investors reassess the risk of renewed U.S.-Iran conflict. Falling volatility, falling yields and falling energy alongside rising equities describe a dovish-repricing drift, not the stress-driven one-way repricing that normally precedes mean-reversion failure. The regional picture conflicts: the Hang Seng fell 3% to an 11-week low near 23,900 with technology under particular pressure, the Nikkei lost 0.9% and the TOPIX 1%, while the KOSPI gained 0.5% and the ASX 200 0.8%. European cash indices each trade about 0.2% higher but the STOXX 600 is on course for its worst week since mid-April, down close to 2%, as the French 10-year OAT reaches its highest since 2002 and the French-German spread widens beyond 140 basis points, the widest since the 2012 euro-area crisis. Conflicting cross-asset evidence of this kind raises uncertainty rather than Tail. The dominant scheduled checkpoint is the September employment report at 12:30Z, with consensus near 89,000-90,000 jobs, the unemployment rate seen steady at 4.1% and average hourly earnings near 0.2% month over month, followed by August Factory Orders at 14:00Z. Mode is trend-up because the NQ structure itself is now a one-sided advance from the overnight low with price near the high, even though the amplifier set around it is decaying. The shared Finviz context file was collected on September 29 at 23:14Z, far outside the 90-minute freshness limit and marked partial with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was treated as stale and contributed nothing to this assessment.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding published Claude hours stayed inside the watch band. Tail opened the window at 20% in the 08:00Z hour on October 1, peaked at 24% during the 14:00Z hour, then printed 20% for fifteen consecutive hours before stepping to 21% in the 07:00Z hour. Stress rose from 75% to a 79% overnight peak as the long-end yield selloff intensified, held 78-79% through the Asian session and eased to 77% at the end of the window, while Confidence stayed between 87% and 89% throughout.
outlookSummary: The forecast holds Tail at 23% through the European morning while the widened overnight band is assumed to keep containing price, steps it to 24% in the release hour as depth thins, and reaches the 25% block threshold only conditionally for the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots covering post-release repricing and the U.S. cash open. That elevation is contingent on an aligned opening auction, pullbacks that fail and a long-end yield break back above the 5.345% peak, not on the release itself. Tail then eases back through the afternoon as repricing is assumed to complete, reaching the 20% floor at the 21:00Z CME weekend halt. Stress peaks in the extreme band at 83% around the post-release hour and decays to a 60% weekend floor that still carries the unresolved European fiscal and long-end yield backdrop. From 21:00Z no live price path can form, so the final eleven slots hold the 20% floor while Confidence steps down to mark a carried rather than observed assessment. The next live reference is the Sunday reopen near 22:00Z and the next scheduled checkpoints are the S&P Global Services PMI final and ISM Services on 5 October, all outside this horizon.
